_readme: EVERY word and sentence the home-page typing test can produce lives in this file.
Edit it freely - nothing here is generated, and no text is hardcoded anywhere else.
words   : the general word bank for the time / words modes.
quotes  : the quote mode. `text` is typed, `source` is printed under the result.
bands   : which school grades count as primary / middle / senior.
subjects: the `subject` mode. Keys are the subject SLUGS from lib/k12.ts
(the English name, lowercased and hyphenated) - the same keys its
SUBJECT_ART table uses, so a subject is named once for the whole app.
A key may carry a band suffix - "mathematics@primary" next to
"mathematics" - so young children can get easier sentences.
Each language block holds `words` and `sentences`. The test prefers a sentence;
if a subject has none it builds a word drill instead. Latin script only (en/uz):
the on-screen keyboard is US QWERTY, so Cyrillic would light up nothing.
Two things to know before editing:
- There is no grade picker on the home page any more, so ALL bands of a
subject are POOLED into one pot. The band suffix is kept for the day a
picker returns; today it changes nothing about what a learner sees.
- The config bar offers only the five subjects listed in FEATURED_SUBJECTS
(lib/typingTest.ts). Every other subject here is written and checked but
unreachable until that list names it. Add to that list, not just here.

en.text: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
Simplicity is the soul of efficiency.
It always seems impossible until it is done.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
The only way to learn a new programming language is by writing programs in it. The first program to write is the same for all languages: print the words hello world.

Practice does not make perfect. Only perfect practice makes perfect. If you practise a thing the wrong way, you will get very good at doing it wrong, and that is much harder to undo than to learn it well the first time.

We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit. The hand that has learned a movement well no longer needs the eye to guide it, and the mind is free at last to think about the thing it wanted to say.

The computer is a bicycle for the mind. It does not think for you, and it never will. What it does is take the small, slow, repeated work off your hands, so that the part of you that is genuinely rare, the part that has ideas, is the only part still doing any work. A tool is good exactly when it disappears while you use it, and you are left alone with the problem you actually care about solving.

Reading is a conversation. All books talk. But a good book listens as well. When you have read enough of them, you begin to notice that the words on the page arrive faster than you can say them aloud, and that is when reading stops being work and starts being thinking. Typing is the same skill turned around: the fingers stop being in the way, and the sentence goes straight from the head to the screen.

Mashq qilish yetarli emas, to'g'ri mashq qilish kerak. Agar bir ishni noto'g'ri takrorlasang, sen o'sha ishni noto'g'ri qilishga usta bo'lasan. Buni keyin tuzatish esa boshidan to'g'ri o'rganishdan ko'ra ancha qiyin bo'ladi. Shuning uchun sekin, lekin xatosiz boshla; tezlik keyin o'zi keladi.
